Multiple RMM agents co-resident on one host (BlueDash redundant access) AIInstallation Medium
Detects two or more distinct RMM families (ScreenConnect + Level + Tactical RMM/MeshAgent) appearing on the same endpoint within a short window — the BlueDash resilience pattern of stacking RMM tools so removal of one leaves access intact. Rationale: The article explicitly states Level RMM + ConnectWise ScreenConnect are dropped in parallel and a sibling repo adds Tactical RMM, framed as deliberate redundant access. Counting distinct RMM families per host targets that stacking behaviour rather than any single tool, which alone can be legitimate. Cross-checked against: • https://www.microsoft.com/en-us/security/blog/2026/03/03/signed-malware-impersonating-workplace-apps-deploys-rmm-backdoors/ • https://redcanary.com/blog/threat-intelligence/phishing-rmm-tools/
ATT&CKT1219 T1078
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • MSP migrating a client from one RMM (e.g. ScreenConnect) to another (e.g. Tactical RMM) leaving both temporarily installed
  • Sanctioned IT stack that genuinely runs two RMM/remote-support tools
  • MeshAgent bundled by Tactical RMM counted as a separate family (tune the family mapping)
  • Security tooling that embeds a MeshAgent-derived component
Suppression filter
| where DeviceName !in~ (dynamic([]))  // add sanctioned dual-RMM hosts / MSP-migration assets to this allowlist
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm whether both RMM families are sanctioned for this host — check asset inventory and the installing parent process (unsigned/%TEMP% install = malicious). 2) Contain: if unsanctioned, isolate, uninstall all rogue agents, and block their C2/enrollment endpoints. 3) Hunt: pivot to UC3 for the Level enrollment key and UC5 for recon commands run through the RMM context; check other hosts touched by the same installing user.
let RmmBins = dynamic(["screenconnect.clientservice.exe","screenconnect.windowsclient.exe","tacticalrmm.exe","meshagent.exe","level.exe","level-windows-amd64.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| extend fn = tolower(FileName)
| where fn in (RmmBins) or ProcessCommandLine has "LEVEL_API_KEY"
| extend RmmFamily = case(
    fn startswith "screenconnect", "ScreenConnect",
    fn in ("tacticalrmm.exe","meshagent.exe"), "TacticalRMM",
    fn startswith "level" or ProcessCommandLine has "LEVEL_API_KEY", "LevelRMM",
    "Other")
| summarize Families = make_set(RmmFamily), FamilyCount = dcount(RmmFamily), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp), SampleCmds = make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 5) by DeviceName
| where FamilyCount >= 2   // 2+ distinct RMM families on one host = redundant-access pattern
| order by LastSeen desc
let RmmBins = dynamic(["screenconnect.clientservice.exe","screenconnect.windowsclient.exe","tacticalrmm.exe","meshagent.exe","level.exe","level-windows-amd64.exe"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend fn = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where fn in (RmmBins) or CommandLine has "LEVEL_API_KEY"
| extend RmmFamily = case(
    fn startswith "screenconnect", "ScreenConnect",
    fn in ("tacticalrmm.exe","meshagent.exe"), "TacticalRMM",
    fn startswith "level" or CommandLine has "LEVEL_API_KEY", "LevelRMM",
    "Other")
| summarize Families = make_set(RmmFamily), FamilyCount = dcount(RmmFamily), FirstSeen = min(TimeGenerated), LastSeen = max(TimeGenerated) by Computer
| where FamilyCount >= 2
| order by LastSeen desc
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 (@Image:(*\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe OR *\screenconnect.clientservice.exe OR *\ScreenConnect.WindowsClient.exe OR *\tacticalrmm.exe OR *\TacticalRMM.exe OR *\meshagent.exe OR *\MeshAgent.exe OR *\level.exe OR *\Level.exe) OR @CommandLine:*LEVEL_API_KEY*)
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2
| ImageFileName=/(screenconnect\.(clientservice|windowsclient)|tacticalrmm|meshagent|level(-windows-amd64)?)\.exe$/i OR CommandLine=/LEVEL_API_KEY/i
| case { ImageFileName=/screenconnect/i | fam:="ScreenConnect"; ImageFileName=/(tacticalrmm|meshagent)/i | fam:="TacticalRMM"; * | fam:="LevelRMM"; }
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName], function=collect([fam]))
| famcount:=count(fam, distinct=true, as=famcount)
| famcount>=2
ENDPOINT

| tstats `summariesonly` values(Processes.process_name) as procs values(Processes.process) as cmds min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ScreenConnect.WindowsClient.exe","tacticalrmm.exe","meshagent.exe","level.exe","level-windows-amd64.exe") OR Processes.process="*LEVEL_API_KEY*") by Processes.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | eval fam=0 | eval fam=if(match(mvjoin(procs,","),"(?i)screenconnect"),fam+1,fam) | eval fam=if(match(mvjoin(procs,","),"(?i)(tacticalrmm|meshagent)"),fam+1,fam) | eval fam=if(match(mvjoin(procs,","),"(?i)level") OR match(mvjoin(cmds,","),"LEVEL_API_KEY"),fam+1,fam) | where fam>=2 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false values(Processes.process_name) as procs values(Processes.process) as cmds min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where (Processes.process_name IN ("ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ScreenConnect.WindowsClient.exe","tacticalrmm.exe","meshagent.exe","level.exe","level-windows-amd64.exe") OR Processes.process="*LEVEL_API_KEY*") by Processes.dest | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | eval fam=0 | eval fam=if(match(mvjoin(procs,","),"(?i)screenconnect"),fam+1,fam) | eval fam=if(match(mvjoin(procs,","),"(?i)(tacticalrmm|meshagent)"),fam+1,fam) | eval fam=if(match(mvjoin(procs,","),"(?i)level") OR match(mvjoin(cmds,","),"LEVEL_API_KEY"),fam+1,fam) | where fam>=2 | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Host reconnaissance sequence spawned from an RMM agent context (BlueDash operator checklist) AIActions on Objectives Medium
Detects the BlueDash post-install discovery checklist — reboot-pending check, BitLocker/system-volume status, firewall-profile enumeration and local Administrators enumeration — when the parent process is an RMM agent rather than an approved IT workflow. This is the behavioural opportunity ZeroBEC highlighted. Rationale: Maps the article's explicit operator checklist (reboot-pending, system-volume/BitLocker protection, firewall profiles, local Administrators membership) to their canonical Windows commands, gated on an RMM parent — the exact 'unauthorized RMM context vs approved IT workflow' distinction ZeroBEC called out as the detection opportunity. Cross-checked against: • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/operation-bluedash-deploys-level-rmm.html • https://redcanary.com/blog/threat-intelligence/phishing-rmm-tools/
ATT&CKT1069.001 T1518.001 T1082 T1016
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Sanctioned MSP running the same triage commands via ScreenConnect/Tactical RMM during legitimate support
  • Automated RMM monitoring scripts polling BitLocker or firewall status as health checks
  • Patch-readiness tooling checking PendingFileRenameOperations before reboot
  • Helpdesk technician enumerating local admins to fix a user permission issue
Suppression filter
| where AccountName !endswith "$" and DeviceName !in~ (dynamic([]))  // allowlist sanctioned MSP/RMM-managed hosts here
Response runbook
1) Triage: verify the RMM agent itself is sanctioned (cross-check UC4); if the agent is rogue, every child command is malicious. 2) Contain: isolate the host, terminate the RMM session, and preserve the process tree for the operator command sequence. 3) Hunt: look for follow-on privilege escalation or lateral movement from the same session and confirm whether the recon preceded additional payload staging or account manipulation.
let RmmParents = dynamic(["screenconnect.clientservice.exe","screenconnect.windowsclient.exe","tacticalrmm.exe","meshagent.exe","level.exe"]);
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where tolower(InitiatingProcessFileName) in (RmmParents)
| extend Cmd = tolower(ProcessCommandLine)
| where (FileName in~ ("net.exe","net1.exe") and Cmd has "localgroup" and Cmd has "admin")
    or (FileName =~ "manage-bde.exe" and Cmd has "-status")
    or (FileName =~ "netsh.exe" and Cmd has_all ("advfirewall","show"))
    or (FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and Cmd has_any ("get-bitlockervolume","get-localgroupmember","pendingfilerenameoperations","win32_shadowcopy","netfirewallprofile"))
| summarize Recon = make_set(ProcessCommandLine, 10), ReconTypes = dcount(FileName), FirstSeen = min(Timestamp), LastSeen = max(Timestamp) by DeviceName, AccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by LastSeen desc
let RmmParents = dynamic(["screenconnect.clientservice.exe","screenconnect.windowsclient.exe","tacticalrmm.exe","meshagent.exe","level.exe"]);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| extend pfn = tolower(tostring(split(ParentProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| extend cfn = tolower(tostring(split(NewProcessName, "\\")[-1]))
| where pfn in (RmmParents)
| extend Cmd = tolower(CommandLine)
| where (cfn in ("net.exe","net1.exe") and Cmd has "localgroup" and Cmd has "admin")
    or (cfn == "manage-bde.exe" and Cmd has "-status")
    or (cfn == "netsh.exe" and Cmd has "advfirewall" and Cmd has "show")
    or (cfn in ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe") and Cmd has_any ("get-bitlockervolume","get-localgroupmember","pendingfilerenameoperations","netfirewallprofile"))
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, ParentProcessName, NewProcessName, CommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: Discovery Commands Spawned by RMM Agent (Operation BlueDash)
id: 4c9b0f77-2e63-4a15-b8d0-9f1e2a3b4c55
description: Detects local-admin, firewall, BitLocker and reboot-pending discovery commands whose parent is an RMM agent
references:
  - https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/operation-bluedash-deploys-level-rmm.html
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/27
tags:
  - attack.t1069.001
  - attack.t1518.001
  - attack.t1082
logsource:
  category: process_creation
  product: windows
detection:
  parent:
    ParentImage|endswith:
      - '\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe'
      - '\ScreenConnect.WindowsClient.exe'
      - '\tacticalrmm.exe'
      - '\meshagent.exe'
      - '\level.exe'
  recon_localadmin:
    Image|endswith:
      - '\net.exe'
      - '\net1.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'localgroup'
      - 'admin'
  recon_bitlocker:
    Image|endswith: '\manage-bde.exe'
    CommandLine|contains: '-status'
  recon_firewall:
    Image|endswith: '\netsh.exe'
    CommandLine|contains|all:
      - 'advfirewall'
      - 'show'
  condition: parent and (recon_localadmin or recon_bitlocker or recon_firewall)
level: medium
source:windows.sysmon @EventID:1 @ParentImage:(*\ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe OR *\ScreenConnect.WindowsClient.exe OR *\tacticalrmm.exe OR *\TacticalRMM.exe OR *\meshagent.exe OR *\MeshAgent.exe OR *\level.exe OR *\Level.exe) (@CommandLine:(*localgroup* *admin* OR *"advfirewall show"* OR *"manage-bde"*status* OR *Get-BitLockerVolume* OR *Get-LocalGroupMember* OR *PendingFileRenameOperations*))
#event_simpleName=ProcessRollup2 ParentBaseFileName=/(screenconnect\.(clientservice|windowsclient)|tacticalrmm|meshagent|level)\.exe$/i
| CommandLine=/(localgroup.*admin|advfirewall\s+show|manage-bde.*-status|get-bitlockervolume|get-localgroupmember|pendingfilerenameoperations)/i
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ParentBaseFileName, CommandLine], function=count())
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count values(Processes.process) as cmds min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ScreenConnect.WindowsClient.exe","tacticalrmm.exe","meshagent.exe","level.exe") AND (Processes.process_name IN ("net.exe","net1.exe","manage-bde.exe","netsh.exe") OR Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where like(process,"%localgroup%administ%") OR like(process,"%manage-bde%status%") OR like(process,"%advfirewall show allprofiles%") OR like(process,"%Get-BitLockerVolume%") OR like(process,"%Get-LocalGroupMember%") OR like(process,"%PendingFileRenameOperations%") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
| tstats summariesonly=false count values(Processes.process) as cmds min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("ScreenConnect.ClientService.exe","ScreenConnect.WindowsClient.exe","tacticalrmm.exe","meshagent.exe","level.exe") AND (Processes.process_name IN ("net.exe","net1.exe","manage-bde.exe","netsh.exe") OR Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe")) by Processes.dest Processes.user Processes.parent_process_name Processes.process_name Processes.process | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)` | where like(process,"%localgroup%administ%") OR like(process,"%manage-bde%status%") OR like(process,"%advfirewall show allprofiles%") OR like(process,"%Get-BitLockerVolume%") OR like(process,"%Get-LocalGroupMember%") OR like(process,"%PendingFileRenameOperations%") | convert ctime(firstTime) ctime(lastTime)
Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

    [| tstats summariesonly=false earliest(_time) AS exec_time

                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]
| tstats summariesonly=false count
    from datamodel=Email.All_Email
    where All_Email.file_name!="-"
    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats summariesonly=false count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process
     | rename Processes.user as user]

Microsoft Teams external-tenant chat from unverified IT-helpdesk impersonator Delivery High
External Teams chat where displayName contains 'helpdesk' or 'IT support' — common 2024+ vishing pattern (Storm-1811, Black Basta, UNC6692). No CIM data model maps to Teams chats; uses raw O365 audit logs.
ATT&CKT1566.004 T1566
Data sourcesCloudAppEvents
CloudAppEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where Application == "Microsoft Teams"
| where ActionType == "MessageSent"
| where RawEventData has "ExternalParticipants"
| extend SenderDisplayName = tostring(parse_json(RawEventData).SenderDisplayName)
| where SenderDisplayName matches regex @"(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)"
| project Timestamp, AccountDisplayName, IPAddress, ActivityType, SenderDisplayName, RawEventData
// External Teams chat — Teams audit lives in OfficeActivity.
OfficeActivity
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where OfficeWorkload == "MicrosoftTeams"
| where Operation in~ ("MessageSent","ChatCreated","TeamsImpersonationDetected")
| where isnotempty(UserId)
| where Subject has_any ("IT","helpdesk","support","password","verify")
   or Recipients has_any ("IT","helpdesk")
| project TimeGenerated, UserId, Operation, Subject, Recipients,
          ClientIP, UserAgent
| order by TimeGenerated desc
CLOUD
`o365_management_activity`
  Workload=MicrosoftTeams Operation=MessageSent
  ExternalParticipants=*
| where match(SenderDisplayName, "(?i)(help.?desk|it.?support|service.?desk|tech.?support|admin)")
| stats count, earliest(_time) as firstTime, latest(_time) as lastTime
    by SenderUpn, SenderDisplayName, RecipientUpn, ChatId

Cruciferra persistence: Run key 'putty' value pointing to non-PuTTY binary AIInstallation High
Hunts Cruciferra's fixed persistence artifact: a HKCU/HKLM CurrentVersion\Run value named 'putty' whose data does NOT reference the legitimate putty.exe. This is a hard-coded decoy value name the crypter writes on every host, making it a high-fidelity anchor independent of payload family. Rationale: 'putty' Run-key value name is a fixed Cruciferra artifact named verbatim by Proofpoint/THN; the not-putty.exe filter removes legitimate PuTTY autostart while keeping the decoy. Cross-checked Proofpoint and Infosecurity-Magazine write-ups. Cross-checked against: • https://www.proofpoint.com/us/blog/threat-insight/unpacking-cruciferra-analysis-sophisticated-crypter-service • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/cruciferra-crypter-process-ghosting/
ATT&CKT1547.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Registry
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Admin manually creates a Run entry literally named 'putty' pointing to a custom launcher script (rare)
  • Software packagers that register a 'putty' autostart wrapper without the .exe suffix in Details
  • GPO/SCCM deployment tooling writing a 'putty' shortcut launcher
  • Portable-app managers that rename PuTTY and register it under a generic 'putty' value
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\Temp\", @"\AppData\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Users\Public\") or RegistryValueData has_any (@"\Temp\", @"\AppData\", @"\ProgramData\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: pull RegistryValueData to see the actual autorun target path; if it is under \Temp, \ProgramData, \AppData or Public and is not putty.exe, treat as malicious. 2) Contain: isolate host, kill and quarantine the referenced binary, delete the Run value. 3) Hunt: sweep the org for the same 'putty' Run value, and on the confirmed host pivot to DeviceImageLoadEvents for GoFlyDrv.sys/other BYOVD drivers and DeviceNetworkEvents for the Cruciferra C2 IOCs.
DeviceRegistryEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("RegistryValueSet","RegistryKeyCreated")
| where RegistryKey has @"CurrentVersion\Run"
| where RegistryValueName =~ "putty"
| where isempty(RegistryValueData) or RegistryValueData !contains "putty.exe"
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, RegistryKey, RegistryValueName, RegistryValueData, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessSHA256
| order by Timestamp desc
ImRegistryEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where RegistryKey has @"CurrentVersion\Run"
| where RegistryValue =~ "putty"
| where isempty(RegistryValueData) or RegistryValueData !contains "putty.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, RegistryKey, RegistryValue, RegistryValueData, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cruciferra BYOVD: vulnerable driver (GoFlyDrv.sys) load for EDR tampering AIInstallation High
Hunts the load of the specific legitimate-but-vulnerable kernel drivers Cruciferra drops to terminate security processes: GoFlyDrv.sys plus the helper set Core64.sys, HwOs2Ec.sys, LnvMSRIO.MemoryInformer.sys and NTIOLib_X64.sys. Flags them when loaded from outside the canonical System32\drivers path. Rationale: GoFlyDrv.sys is named in the article; the helper driver set (Core64.sys, HwOs2Ec.sys, LnvMSRIO.MemoryInformer.sys, NTIOLib_X64.sys) was confirmed by Proofpoint's blog via the search. Loading these signed-but-vulnerable drivers from outside System32\drivers is a strong BYOVD signal. Cross-checked against: • https://www.proofpoint.com/us/blog/threat-insight/unpacking-cruciferra-analysis-sophisticated-crypter-service • https://gbhackers.com/cruciferra-crypter-to-disable-edr/
ATT&CKT1562.001 T1211
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate MSI Afterburner / hardware-monitoring installs loading NTIOLib_X64.sys from their own program directory
  • Lenovo Vantage / firmware tools loading LnvMSRIO or HwOs2Ec drivers from vendor paths
  • Security researcher / malware-analysis VM intentionally loading vulnerable drivers
  • Overclocking utilities that ship Core64.sys
Suppression filter
| where not (InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\MSI Afterburner\", @"\Lenovo\", @"\Program Files\") and FolderPath has_any (@"\Program Files\", @"\Program Files (x86)\"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the InitiatingProcess that dropped/loaded the driver and its folder path; a driver in \Temp/\ProgramData loaded by an unsigned or Mono-based process is malicious. 2) Contain: isolate host, stop and delete the driver service, quarantine the loading binary; check whether AV/EDR processes were killed. 3) Hunt: correlate to the 'putty' Run-key persistence, Process-Ghosting file deletes, and C2 IOC connections; block the driver hashes org-wide via WDAC/ASR and confirm the Microsoft vulnerable-driver blocklist is enforced.
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName in~ ("GoFlyDrv.sys","Core64.sys","HwOs2Ec.sys","LnvMSRIO.MemoryInformer.sys","NTIOLib_X64.sys")
| where FolderPath !contains @"\Windows\System32\drivers\"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType == "FileCreated"
| where TargetFileName in~ ("GoFlyDrv.sys","Core64.sys","HwOs2Ec.sys","LnvMSRIO.MemoryInformer.sys","NTIOLib_X64.sys")
| where TargetFilePath !contains @"\Windows\System32\drivers\"
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cruciferra loader side-load DLLs and Remcos logs.dat drop AIInstallation Medium
Hunts creation of the named Cruciferra loader/payload DLLs (ALTERNATE.dll, ClassLibrary3.dll, Keylogger.dll) and the msedge_proxy.exe side-load host, plus the Remcos-style artifacts C:\ProgramData\remcos\logs.dat and C:\ProgramData\colors\logs.dat dropped post-execution. These filenames/paths are campaign-specific staging artifacts. Rationale: Side-load DLL names (ALTERNATE.dll, ClassLibrary3.dll, Keylogger.dll), the msedge_proxy.exe side-load host, and the C:\ProgramData\remcos|colors\logs.dat artifacts were confirmed via the Proofpoint/Seqrite Operation DragonReturn reporting; these are campaign-specific filenames unlikely to appear benignly. Cross-checked against: • https://www.proofpoint.com/us/blog/threat-insight/unpacking-cruciferra-analysis-sophisticated-crypter-service • https://www.seqrite.com/blog/operation-dragonreturn-china-nexus-cyber-espionage-campaign-targeting-govt-of-india-mof-tax-infrastructure-via-multi-stage-dcrat-deployment/
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1105
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • A legitimate internal project happening to build a DLL named ClassLibrary3.dll (default Visual Studio project name) in a dev machine's bin folder
  • Chromium-based apps writing a genuine msedge_proxy.exe under Program Files\Microsoft\Edge
  • Backup/restore tools recreating a ProgramData folder tree
  • Security tooling writing decoy logs.dat files
Suppression filter
| where not (FolderPath has_any (@"\Microsoft\Edge\", @"\Program Files\", @"\Program Files (x86)\") and InitiatingProcessFolderPath has @"\Program Files\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: check the InitiatingProcess and folder path — ClassLibrary3.dll/Keylogger.dll outside a Program Files signed vendor path, or msedge_proxy.exe outside \Microsoft\Edge\, is malicious. 2) Contain: isolate host, quarantine the DLL and its side-loading EXE host, and delete the logs.dat keylog store. 3) Hunt: pivot to the parent EXE side-loading the DLL, the 'putty' Run key, and outbound C2 to the Cruciferra IOC set; sweep for the same filenames org-wide.
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where ActionType in ("FileCreated","FileModified","FileRenamed")
| where (FileName in~ ("ALTERNATE.dll","ClassLibrary3.dll","Keylogger.dll","msedge_proxy.exe"))
    or (FileName =~ "logs.dat" and FolderPath has_any (@"\ProgramData\remcos\", @"\ProgramData\colors\"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessAccountName
| order by Timestamp desc
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventType in ("FileCreated","FileModified")
| where (TargetFileName in~ ("ALTERNATE.dll","ClassLibrary3.dll","Keylogger.dll","msedge_proxy.exe"))
    or (TargetFileName =~ "logs.dat" and TargetFilePath has_any (@"\ProgramData\remcos\", @"\ProgramData\colors\"))
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, TargetFileSHA256, ActingProcessName, ActingProcessCommandLine
| order by TimeGenerated desc

Cruciferra known-sample SHA256 execution/write AIExploitation Medium
Direct IOC match on the 20 Cruciferra SHA256 sample hashes from the reporting, on either process execution or file write. Zero-tolerance alerting rule for confirmed samples. Rationale: 20 SHA256 sample hashes ship with the article's IOC bundle for Cruciferra; hash matches are unambiguous. Because the crypter is polymorphic per-sample these will decay, so pair with the behavioral UCs. Cross-checked against: • https://www.proofpoint.com/us/blog/threat-insight/unpacking-cruciferra-analysis-sophisticated-crypter-service • https://thehackernews.com/2026/07/cruciferra-crypter-uses-byovd-and.html
ATT&CKT1027.010 T1204.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Analyst/IR sandbox detonation of the sample on a corporate host
  • EDR/AV quarantine copy re-hashing the file (write event, not execution)
  • Threat-intel feed replication copying sample files across a research share
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the event is execution (not a quarantine/analysis copy); check DeviceName against known sandbox hosts. 2) Contain: isolate host, quarantine binary, kill process tree, and add hashes to the org blocklist. 3) Hunt: because Cruciferra re-encrypts per sample, immediately pivot from the confirmed host to the behavioral IOCs — 'putty' Run key, BYOVD driver load, C2 IOC network — to catch polymorphic variants the hash rule will miss.

Cruciferra C2 beacon to known IOC domains/IPs (incl. .gu.cc cluster) AICommand & Control Medium
Hunts network/DNS resolution to the Cruciferra C2 infrastructure: the fixed IP set, the algorithmically-named .gu.cc dynamic-DNS subdomain cluster, DuckDNS host, and other campaign domains. Network pivot distinct from the host-based UCs. Rationale: C2 IPs, campaign domains, and the distinctive algorithmically-named *.gu.cc subdomain cluster come from the article IOC bundle sourced from Proofpoint. The .gu.cc cluster (10+ random-string subdomains on one free DDNS parent) is a strong DGA-style anchor. Note: individual IOCs corroborated only against the Proofpoint blog; treat low-and-slow single hits as leads. Cross-checked against: • https://www.proofpoint.com/us/blog/threat-insight/unpacking-cruciferra-analysis-sophisticated-crypter-service • https://socprime.com/active-threats/cruciferra-analyzing-a-sophisticated-crypter-service/
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1568.002
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Legitimate but unrelated site hosted on the shared gu.cc free-DNS parent (broad .gu.cc match)
  • Security tooling / TI enrichment sandbox resolving IOC domains during analysis
  • A shared-hosting IP later re-purposed to a benign service (IP reuse over time)
  • DNS sinkhole or proxy pre-resolving blocked domains for logging
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe") or InitiatingProcessFolderPath has_any (@"\Temp\", @"\AppData\", @"\ProgramData\")
Response runbook
1) Triage: identify the InitiatingProcess making the connection — a Mono/side-loaded or ProgramData-resident process beaconing to these hosts is malicious; browser hits to a single .gu.cc host may be incidental. 2) Contain: block the domains/IPs at proxy/firewall, isolate the beaconing host. 3) Hunt: on the host, pivot to the loader DLLs, 'putty' Run key, and BYOVD driver; extract additional infra by pivoting on the parent PID's other connections.
let C2Domains = dynamic(["govtop.one","ikkkkddd.com","1kkkkddd.com","kkxqbh.top","simaqz.com","jiayingjing.com","gatuso.duckdns.org","0zbqnac1t4dv2t2wuodv1m.com","almacensantangel.com","hsahyteiows.gu.cc","yicoweytcbtw.gu.cc","nciyeyrawoe.gu.cc","lasiduutfe.gu.cc","xkcifgieusr.gu.cc","viuyeyrwqs.gu.cc","pmcjsuyraw.gu.cc","laiwutrencr.gu.cc","maisytawe.gu.cc","kawosyetw.gu.cc","nviuawusye.gu.cc"]);
let C2IPs = dynamic(["89.34.90.99","204.194.48.250","118.107.0.197","27.50.54.191","223.26.63.40","117.44.201.119"]);
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where RemoteIP in (C2IPs) or RemoteUrl in~ (C2Domains) or (RemoteUrl endswith ".gu.cc")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, RemoteUrl, RemoteIP, RemotePort, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc

Process Ghosting: executable created then deleted while backing a live process AIInstallation Medium
Behavioral hunt for Cruciferra's Process Ghosting variant — a temporary image file is created and unlinked from disk around process launch so EDR memory scanners have nothing to scan. Correlates a FileCreated + FileDeleted of the same .exe/.dll in a user-writable staging path by the same process within a tight window. Rationale: Process Ghosting is the article's headline technique (create-then-delete the image backing a running process). Same-PID create+delete of an .exe/.dll in a staging path within 2 minutes is a workable behavioral proxy since Defender/Sysmon do not directly surface the NtSetInformationFile(DELETE) primitive. Hunting tier due to installer/self-update noise. Cross-checked against: • https://www.proofpoint.com/us/blog/threat-insight/unpacking-cruciferra-analysis-sophisticated-crypter-service • https://www.infosecurity-magazine.com/news/cruciferra-crypter-process-ghosting/
ATT&CKT1036.004 T1055.013
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: medium — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Software installers extracting a temp EXE/DLL then cleaning it up (Squirrel, NSIS, MSI custom actions)
  • Application self-update routines staging and deleting update payloads in AppData
  • Browser/Electron apps writing and removing temporary module caches
  • Antivirus scanning that copies then deletes a temp scan artifact
  • Build/CI agents on developer hosts creating and removing temp binaries
Suppression filter
| where CreatorProc !in~ ("msiexec.exe","setup.exe","update.exe","squirrel.exe","7z.exe","7zg.exe") and not (FolderPath has @"\AppData\Local\Temp\" and CreatorProc has_any ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","teams.exe"))
Response runbook
1) Triage: sort by shortest LifeSec — a sub-5-second create/delete of an EXE by a Mono/dotnet or side-loaded parent, especially followed by a suspended child process, is high-signal; installers usually run tens of seconds. 2) Contain: isolate host, capture a memory image before reboot (the ghosted payload only lives in RAM), suspend/kill the associated process tree. 3) Hunt: correlate the creating process to the BYOVD driver load, 'putty' Run key, and C2 IOCs; carve the deleted file from the memory image for hashing.
let Window = 2m;
let Created = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where ActionType == "FileCreated"
    | where FolderPath has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Users\Public\")
    | where FileName endswith ".exe" or FileName endswith ".dll"
    | project DeviceId, DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, CreateTime=Timestamp, CreatorProc=InitiatingProcessFileName, CreatorPid=InitiatingProcessId, SHA256;
let Deleted = DeviceFileEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(14d)
    | where ActionType == "FileDeleted"
    | where FileName endswith ".exe" or FileName endswith ".dll"
    | project DeviceId, FileName, FolderPath, DeleteTime=Timestamp, DeleterPid=InitiatingProcessId;
Created
| join kind=inner Deleted on DeviceId, FileName, FolderPath
| where DeleteTime between (CreateTime .. CreateTime + Window)
| where CreatorPid == DeleterPid
| project CreateTime, DeleteTime, LifeSec=datetime_diff('second', DeleteTime, CreateTime), DeviceName, FileName, FolderPath, CreatorProc, SHA256
| order by CreateTime desc
let Window = 2m;
let Created = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where EventType == "FileCreated"
    | where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\AppData\Local\Temp\", @"\ProgramData\", @"\Users\Public\")
    | where TargetFileName endswith ".exe" or TargetFileName endswith ".dll"
    | project DvcHostname, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, CreateTime=TimeGenerated, CreatorProc=ActingProcessName, CreatorPid=ActingProcessId;
let Deleted = ImFileEvent
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(14d)
    | where EventType == "FileDeleted"
    | where TargetFileName endswith ".exe" or TargetFileName endswith ".dll"
    | project DvcHostname, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, DeleteTime=TimeGenerated, DeleterPid=ActingProcessId;
Created
| join kind=inner Deleted on DvcHostname, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath
| where DeleteTime between (CreateTime .. CreateTime + Window)
| where CreatorPid == DeleterPid
| project CreateTime, DeleteTime, LifeSec=datetime_diff('second', DeleteTime, CreateTime), DvcHostname, TargetFileName, TargetFilePath, CreatorProc
| order by CreateTime desc
#event_simpleName=/^File(Written|Deleted)$/ (TargetFileName=/\\(AppData\\Local\\Temp|ProgramData|Users\\Public)\\/i TargetFileName=/\.(exe|dll)$/i)
| groupBy([aid, ComputerName, ContextProcessId, TargetFileName], function=collect([event_simpleName]))
| event_simpleName=/FileWritten/ AND event_simpleName=/FileDeleted/
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` values(Filesystem.action) as actions min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime dc(Filesystem.action) as action_variety from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\ProgramData\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Users\\Public\\*") AND (Filesystem.file_name="*.exe" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.dll") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_guid 
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` 
| where like(actions,"%created%") AND like(actions,"%deleted%") 
| eval window_sec=round((lastTime-firstTime),0) | where window_sec<=120 
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
| tstats summariesonly=false values(Filesystem.action) as actions min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime dc(Filesystem.action) as action_variety from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem where (Filesystem.file_path="*\\AppData\\Local\\Temp\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\ProgramData\\*" OR Filesystem.file_path="*\\Users\\Public\\*") AND (Filesystem.file_name="*.exe" OR Filesystem.file_name="*.dll") by Filesystem.dest Filesystem.file_name Filesystem.file_path Filesystem.process_guid 
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)` 
| where like(actions,"%created%") AND like(actions,"%deleted%") 
| eval window_sec=round((lastTime-firstTime),0) | where window_sec<=120 
| `security_content_ctime(firstTime)` | `security_content_ctime(lastTime)`
Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations Command & Control Medium
C2 channel detection via inter-beacon-time stddev / fan-out to single dest.
ATT&CKT1071.001 T1071.004
Data sourcesNetwork_Traffic.All_Traffic DeviceNetworkEvents
DeviceNetworkEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(1d)
| where RemoteIPType == "Public" and ActionType == "ConnectionSuccess"
| project DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort, Timestamp
| sort by DeviceName asc, RemoteIP asc, RemotePort asc, Timestamp asc
| extend prev_dev = prev(DeviceName, 1), prev_ip = prev(RemoteIP, 1),
         prev_port = prev(RemotePort, 1), prev_ts = prev(Timestamp, 1)
| where DeviceName == prev_dev and RemoteIP == prev_ip and RemotePort == prev_port
| extend delta_sec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, prev_ts)
| summarize conn_count = count(), avg_delta = avg(delta_sec), stdev_delta = stdev(delta_sec)
    by DeviceName, RemoteIP, RemotePort
| where conn_count > 30 and avg_delta between (30.0 .. 600.0) and stdev_delta < 5.0
| order by conn_count desc
ImNetworkSession
| where TimeGenerated > ago(2h)
| where DvcAction != "Block"
| where ipv4_is_private(DstIpAddr) == false
| summarize ConnCount = count(),
            DistinctMinutes = dcount(bin(TimeGenerated, 1m))
            by DvcHostname, DstIpAddr, DstPortNumber
| where ConnCount > 50 and DistinctMinutes > 30   // sustained, not bursty
| order by ConnCount desc
NETWORK
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time
| stats avg(delta) AS avg_delta stdev(delta) AS sd_delta count by src, dest
| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count
| tstats summariesonly=false count, values(All_Traffic.dest_port) AS ports
    from datamodel=Network_Traffic.All_Traffic
    where All_Traffic.action="allowed" AND All_Traffic.dest_category!="internal"
    by _time span=10s, All_Traffic.src, All_Traffic.dest
| `drop_dm_object_name(All_Traffic)`
| streamstats current=f last(_time) AS prev_time by src, dest
| eval delta = _time - prev_time

| where count > 30 AND sd_delta < 5 AND avg_delta>=30 AND avg_delta<=600
| sort - count

Infostealer — non-browser process accessing browser cookie/login DBs Actions on Objectives High
Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies SQLite from Chrome/Edge/Firefox.
ATT&CKT1539 T1555.003
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem DeviceFileEvents
DeviceFileEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where InitiatingProcessAccountName !endswith "$"
| where FolderPath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\", @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\", @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where FileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessAccountName, InitiatingProcessFileName, FolderPath, FileName, ActionType

// ASIM ImFileEvent — covers MDE, Sysmon, AuditD, Defender for Cloud, etc.
ImFileEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where ActorUsername !endswith "$"
| where TargetFilePath has_any (@"\Google\Chrome\User Data\",
                                  @"\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\",
                                  @"\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\")
| where TargetFileName in~ ("Login Data","Cookies","logins.json","cookies.sqlite")
| where ActingProcessName !in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
| project TimeGenerated, DvcHostname, ActorUsername, ActingProcessName,
          TargetFilePath, TargetFileName, EventType

title: Infostealer - Non-Browser Process Accessing Browser Credential Stores
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d01
status: experimental
description: |
    Stealers (RedLine, Lumma, Vidar, Atomic) read Login Data / cookies
    SQLite databases from Chrome/Edge/Firefox profile directories. Any
    non-browser process touching these files is a high-fidelity signal.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1539/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1555/003/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1539
    - attack.t1555.003
    - attack.credential-access
logsource:
    category: file_access
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_path:
        TargetFilename|contains:
            - '\Google\Chrome\User Data\'
            - '\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\'
            - '\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\'
    selection_file:
        TargetFilename|endswith:
            - '\Login Data'
            - '\Cookies'
            - '\logins.json'
            - '\cookies.sqlite'
    filter_browser:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\chrome.exe'
            - '\msedge.exe'
            - '\firefox.exe'
            - '\brave.exe'
            - '\opera.exe'
    condition: selection_path and selection_file and not filter_browser
falsepositives:
    - Backup utilities reading user profile files
    - Browser sync agents from non-stock vendors
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Filesystem
    where (Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Google\Chrome\User Data\*\Cookies*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Microsoft\Edge\User Data\*\Login Data*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\logins.json*"
        OR Filesystem.file_path="*\Mozilla\Firefox\Profiles\*\cookies.sqlite*")
      AND NOT Filesystem.process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe","brave.exe","opera.exe")
    by Filesystem.dest, Filesystem.process_name, Filesystem.file_path, Filesystem.user
| `drop_dm_object_name(Filesystem)`
Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution Delivery High
User received an external email containing a URL, clicked it, and within 60 seconds the recipient's endpoint spawned a scripting interpreter or network downloader (PowerShell / cmd / mshta / curl / certutil / bitsadmin). This is the high-fidelity shape — a raw "user clicked an emailed URL" query is too noisy to alert on because every Microsoft 365 tenant generates thousands of legitimate clicks per day. The exec-correlation step suppresses the noise to roughly the rate at which a click actually drives onto-host execution, which is the actionable signal. Pair with UC_PHISH_LINK_BYPASS (Safe Links override) and UC_PHISH_LINK_NEWDOMAIN for orthogonal high-fidelity variants.
ATT&CKT1566.002 T1204.001 T1059.001
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Web Endpoint.Processes EmailEvents EmailUrlInfo UrlClickEvents DeviceProcessEvents
// Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s.
// Far higher fidelity than "every clicked URL" — most legitimate clicks
// never spawn a non-browser child process, so the join eliminates the
// 99% of noise that makes a raw click query unactionable.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectClicks = UrlClickEvents
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | where ActionType in ("ClickAllowed","ClickedThrough")
    | join kind=inner (
        EmailEvents
        | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
        | where DeliveryAction == "Delivered"
        | where EmailDirection == "Inbound"
        | project NetworkMessageId, Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain,
                  RecipientEmailAddress, EmailTimestamp = Timestamp
      ) on NetworkMessageId
    | join kind=leftouter (
        EmailUrlInfo | project NetworkMessageId, Url, UrlDomain
      ) on NetworkMessageId, Url
    | project ClickTime = Timestamp, AccountUpn, IPAddress, Url, UrlDomain,
              Subject, SenderFromAddress, SenderFromDomain, RecipientEmailAddress,
              ActionType;
// Correlate to a non-browser child process spawned within 60 seconds on
// the recipient's device.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                         "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                        "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                        "bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe","curl.exe","wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectClicks on $left.AccountName == $right.AccountUpn
| where Timestamp between (ClickTime .. ClickTime + 60s)
| project ClickTime, ProcessTime = Timestamp,
          DelaySec = datetime_diff('second', Timestamp, ClickTime),
          DeviceName, AccountName, RecipientEmailAddress, SenderFromAddress,
          Subject, Url, UrlDomain, ActionType,
          FileName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName
| order by ClickTime desc
// UrlClickEvents has no clean Sentinel-native equivalent. The detection
// pivots to: Office Send→Receive proximity to SecurityEvent 4688 of a
// non-browser child process. Lower fidelity than the Defender version.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let SuspectMailUsers = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation =~ "Receive"
    | summarize Subject = any(Subject), Sender = any(Sender)
                by MailboxOwnerUPN, MessageId, EmailTime = bin(TimeGenerated, 1m);
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName has_any ("\chrome.exe","\msedge.exe",
                                     "\firefox.exe","\outlook.exe","\brave.exe")
| where NewProcessName has_any ("\powershell.exe","\pwsh.exe","\cmd.exe",
                                  "\mshta.exe","\rundll32.exe","\regsvr32.exe",
                                  "\wscript.exe","\cscript.exe","\bitsadmin.exe",
                                  "\certutil.exe","\curl.exe","\wget.exe")
| join kind=inner SuspectMailUsers on $left.Account == $right.MailboxOwnerUPN
| where TimeGenerated between (EmailTime .. EmailTime + 60s)
| project TimeGenerated, EmailTime, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,
          NewProcessName, CommandLine, Sender, Subject
| order by TimeGenerated desc
WEB
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
``` Phishing-link click that drives endpoint execution within 60s ```
| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS click_time
    from datamodel=Web
    where Web.action="allowed"
    by Web.src, Web.user, Web.dest, Web.url
| `drop_dm_object_name(Web)`
| rename user AS recipient, dest AS clicked_domain, url AS clicked_url
| join type=inner recipient
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
         from datamodel=Email.All_Email
         where All_Email.action="delivered" AND All_Email.url!="-"
         by All_Email.recipient, All_Email.src_user, All_Email.url, All_Email.subject
     | `drop_dm_object_name(All_Email)`
     | rex field=url "https?://(?<email_domain>[^/]+)"
     | rename recipient AS recipient]
| join type=inner src
    [| tstats `summariesonly` earliest(_time) AS exec_time
         values(Processes.process) AS exec_cmd, values(Processes.process_name) AS exec_proc
         from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
         where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("chrome.exe","msedge.exe","firefox.exe",
                                                   "outlook.exe","brave.exe","arc.exe")
           AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","cmd.exe","mshta.exe",
                                            "rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wscript.exe",
                                            "cscript.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe",
                                            "curl.exe","wget.exe")
         by Processes.dest, Processes.user
     | `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
     | rename dest AS src]
| eval delta_sec = exec_time - click_time
| where delta_sec >= 0 AND delta_sec <= 60
| table click_time, exec_time, delta_sec, recipient, src, src_user, subject,
        clicked_domain, clicked_url, exec_proc, exec_cmd
| sort - click_time

Email attachment opened from external sender Delivery High
Attachment delivery + execution by recipient — most common malware initial access.
ATT&CKT1566.001 T1204.002
Data sourcesEmail.All_Email Endpoint.Processes EmailAttachmentInfo DeviceProcessEvents
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MalAttachments = EmailAttachmentInfo
    | where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where AccountName !endswith "$"
    | project NetworkMessageId, RecipientEmailAddress,
              AttachmentFileName = FileName, AttachmentSHA256 = SHA256;
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(LookbackDays)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe",
                      "mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
| join kind=inner MalAttachments on $left.AccountUpn == $right.RecipientEmailAddress
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, ProcessCommandLine,
          InitiatingProcessFileName, AttachmentFileName, AttachmentSHA256
// Sentinel doesn't have an attachment-hash table. Best approximation:
// OfficeActivity Send/Receive activity + correlate to host process spawn.
let LookbackDays = 7d;
let MailWithAttach = OfficeActivity
    | where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
    | where OfficeWorkload == "Exchange"
    | where Operation in~ ("Send","Receive")
    | where isnotempty(MessageId)
    | project EmailTime = TimeGenerated, MailboxOwnerUPN, Sender,
              Recipients, Subject, MessageId;
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(LookbackDays)
| where EventID == 4688
| where ParentProcessName endswith "OUTLOOK.EXE"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\cmd.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\wscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\cscript.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, NewProcessName, CommandLine,
          ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
ENDPOINT

    by All_Email.src_user, All_Email.recipient, All_Email.file_name, All_Email.subject
| rename All_Email.recipient as user
| join type=inner user
    [| tstats `summariesonly` count
        from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
        where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("OUTLOOK.EXE","winword.exe","excel.exe","powerpnt.exe")
          AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe")
        by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

| tstats summariesonly=false count

title: Office Application Spawning Script Host
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d07
status: experimental
description: |
    Word/Excel/Outlook/OneNote spawning powershell, cmd, wscript,
    cscript, mshta, rundll32, regsvr32 — classic macro / embedded-
    object payload signature.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1566/001/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059
    - attack.t1566.001
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:

            - '\powerpnt.exe'

            - '\mspub.exe'
            - '\visio.exe'
    selection_child:

            - '\wscript.exe'

falsepositives:

level: high

      AND Processes.process_name IN ("cmd.exe","powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","wscript.exe","cscript.exe","mshta.exe","rundll32.exe","regsvr32.exe","wmic.exe","bitsadmin.exe","certutil.exe")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.parent_process_name, Processes.process_name, Processes.process

ATT&CKT1204.004 T1059.001
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes DeviceProcessEvents
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(7d)
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| where InitiatingProcessFileName in~ ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
| where FileName in~ ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
| where ProcessCommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(7d)
| where EventID == 4688

| where ParentProcessName endswith "\explorer.exe"
   or ParentProcessName endswith "\RuntimeBroker.exe"
| where NewProcessName endswith "\powershell.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\pwsh.exe"
   or NewProcessName endswith "\mshta.exe"
| where CommandLine matches regex @"(?i)(iex|invoke-expression|frombase64|downloadstring|hxxp|curl |wget )"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, Account, ParentProcessName,

| order by TimeGenerated desc

title: FakeCaptcha / ClickFix - Clipboard-Injected PowerShell from Explorer
id: 7c8b2e10-4d4f-4a8c-9c1f-bf6e2c4a8d06
status: experimental
description: |
    "FakeCaptcha" / "ClickFix" social-engineering: malicious site asks
    user to press Win+R and paste a payload. The result is
    powershell/mshta launched directly from explorer.exe with iex /
    base64 / downloadstring in the command line.
references:
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1059/001/
    - https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1204/002/
author: Clankerusecase
date: 2026/05/02
tags:
    - attack.t1059.001
    - attack.t1204.002
    - attack.execution
logsource:
    category: process_creation
    product: windows
detection:
    selection_parent:
        ParentImage|endswith:
            - '\explorer.exe'
            - '\RuntimeBroker.exe'
    selection_child:
        Image|endswith:
            - '\powershell.exe'
            - '\pwsh.exe'
            - '\mshta.exe'
    selection_cmd:
        CommandLine|contains:
            - 'iex'
            - 'invoke-expression'
            - 'frombase64'
            - 'downloadstring'
            - 'hxxp'
            - 'curl '
            - 'wget '
    condition: selection_parent and selection_child and selection_cmd
falsepositives:
    - IT-driven scripted automation that admins paste-launch
level: high
ENDPOINT
Toggle if your env has no CIM data-model acceleration.
| tstats `summariesonly` count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`
| tstats summariesonly=false count min(_time) as firstTime max(_time) as lastTime
    from datamodel=Endpoint.Processes
    where Processes.parent_process_name IN ("explorer.exe","RuntimeBroker.exe")
      AND Processes.process_name IN ("powershell.exe","pwsh.exe","mshta.exe")
      AND (Processes.process="*iex*" OR Processes.process="*Invoke-Expression*"
        OR Processes.process="*FromBase64*" OR Processes.process="*DownloadString*"
        OR Processes.process="*hxxp*" OR Processes.process="*curl*" OR Processes.process="*wget*")
    by Processes.dest, Processes.user, Processes.process, Processes.parent_process_name
| `drop_dm_object_name(Processes)`

detection:

TELESHIM Abuses Telegram for C2 in Attacks Against Middle East Governments

The Hacker News
2026-07-27 16 use cases 7 techniques 6 kill-chain phases detected

Cybersecurity researchers have flagged fresh malicious cyber activity by a threat actor with ties to East Asia targeting government entities in the Middle East. The intrusions have resulted in the deployment of previously unreported malware families dubbed TELESHIM, MIXEDKEY, and BINDCLOAK, according to Zscaler ThreatLabz. The cybersecurity firm said it detected the campaign earlier this month.

Actions on Objectives
Detected
Reconnaissance. Attacker researches the target — OSINT, scanning, enumeration.
Weaponization. Coupling exploit code with deliverable payload (e.g. weaponized PDF/Office doc, trojanized installer).
Delivery. Transmitting the weapon (phishing email, USB, watering hole, drive-by, malicious ad). → [LLM] ISO-delivered signed RegSchdTask.exe executed from non-standard/removable path · Phishing-link click correlated to endpoint execution · Email attachment opened from external sender
Exploitation. Triggering the exploit — vulnerability/macro/trust abuse to execute code. → Office app spawning script/LOLBin child process · Fake CAPTCHA / clipboard-injected PowerShell (ClickFix / FakeCaptcha) · Article-specific behavioural hunt — TELESHIM Abuses Telegram for C2 in Attacks Against Middle East Governments
Installation. Establishing persistence on the host — backdoor, service, scheduled task, registry key. → [LLM] TELESHIM DLL side-load: RegSchdTask.exe loads rogue AsTaskSched.dll · [LLM] MIXEDKEY encrypted payload: .PCPKEY file dropped on disk · [LLM] TELESHIM/MIXEDKEY/BINDCLOAK known-bad file hash execution · Scheduled task created with suspicious image / encoded args · File hash IOCs — endpoint file/process match
Command & Control. Beacon to attacker infrastructure for control and tasking. → [LLM] Telegram Bot API used for C2 by non-browser/non-messaging process · [LLM] BINDCLOAK C2 beacon to cert.hypersnet.com / ssl.blsouqs.com · Beaconing — periodic outbound to small set of destinations · Network connections to article IPs / domains
Actions on Objectives. Lateral movement, credential dumping, data theft, ransomware, sabotage. → [LLM] TELESHIM/MIXEDKEY sideload host binary beacons to Telegram (C2 + exfil)
ISO-delivered signed RegSchdTask.exe executed from non-standard/removable path AIDelivery Medium
Hunts the campaign's initial access: the legitimate ASUS-signed RegSchdTask.exe run from an ISO mount, user Temp, Downloads or Public dir rather than its real ASUS install directory. Article-specific because this binary is the sideload host used to load the TELESHIM DLL. Rationale: Anchored on the named ASUS sideload host RegSchdTask.exe (arrives via ISO) with a path exclusion — a signed scheduler utility running from Temp/ISO is the article's exact initial-access shape. Cross-checked against: • https://www.zscaler.com/blogs/security-research/targeted-attack-government-entities-middle-east-part-1 • https://gbhackers.com/hackers-hide-c2-traffic-inside-telegram/
ATT&CKT1204.002 T1574.002
Data sourcesEndpoint.Processes
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Genuine ASUS software portable/troubleshooting run from a technician USB
  • Software packaging/repackaging labs staging ASUS utilities in Temp
  • IT deploying ASUS drivers from a network share extracted to a user path
  • Security researcher detonating the sample in a sanctioned sandbox
Suppression filter
| where InitiatingProcessFileName !in~ ("setup.exe","asussetup.exe","asusdownloadlicense.exe")
Response runbook
1) Triage: confirm the SHA256 against the article's hash list and check the parent — a mounted ISO (explorer.exe / DVD drive letter) or archive tool as parent is high-signal. 2) Contain: isolate the host and quarantine the RegSchdTask.exe/AsTaskSched.dll pair from the same folder. 3) Hunt: on the same device pivot to DeviceImageLoadEvents for AsTaskSched.dll and DeviceNetworkEvents to api.telegram.org within the next hour.
DeviceProcessEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where FileName =~ "RegSchdTask.exe"
| where not(FolderPath has_any (@"\Program Files\", @"\Program Files (x86)\", @"\Windows\"))
| where AccountName !endswith "$"
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, AccountName, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, InitiatingProcessCommandLine
| order by Timestamp desc
SecurityEvent
| where TimeGenerated > ago(30d)
| where EventID == 4688
| where NewProcessName endswith @"\RegSchdTask.exe"
| where NewProcessName !has @"\Program Files" and NewProcessName !has @"\Windows\"
| project TimeGenerated, Computer, SubjectUserName, NewProcessName, CommandLine, ParentProcessName
| order by TimeGenerated desc
title: ASUS RegSchdTask.exe Executed From Non-Standard Path (TELESHIM Sideload Host)
id: 6a1f3c22-9b41-4d7e-8f2a-1c9d0e77aa01
description: Legitimate ASUS RegSchdTask.exe launched from a removable/ISO/Temp path, used to side-load the TELESHIM AsTaskSched.dll
references:
  - https://www.zscaler.com/blogs/security-research/targeted-attack-government-entities-middle-east-part-1
author: SOC Detection Engineering
date: 2026/07/27

  - attack.t1574.002

  filter_legit:

      - '\Program Files (x86)\'

  condition: selection and not filter_legit
level: high

| NOT (ImageFileName=/\\(Program Files|Program Files \(x86\)|Windows)\\/i)

TELESHIM DLL side-load: RegSchdTask.exe loads rogue AsTaskSched.dll AIInstallation High
Hunts the TELESHIM sideload event itself — the ASUS RegSchdTask.exe process loading a non-Microsoft AsTaskSched.dll from a non-standard path. This is the moment the 32-bit TELESHIM backdoor gets execution inside a trusted process. Rationale: Uses the exact parent/module pair named by Zscaler (RegSchdTask.exe -> AsTaskSched.dll); an ASUS scheduler loading a DLL of that name is unique to this intrusion. Falcon FDR does not ship a module-load event type, hence empty falcon query. Cross-checked against: • https://www.zscaler.com/blogs/security-research/targeted-attack-government-entities-middle-east-part-1 • https://cybersecuritynews.com/hackers-telegram-bots-secret-backdoor/
ATT&CKT1574.002 T1497
Data sourcesEndpoint.Filesystem
Expected false positives · estimated rate: low — model-assessed, tune to your environment
  • Genuine ASUS utility shipping a same-named helper DLL after a legitimate update
  • QA/reverse-engineering lab replaying the sample
  • Backup/restore repopulating an old ASUS install folder
  • EDR sensor re-baselining image loads after agent upgrade
Suppression filter
| where not(SHA256 in~ ("")) or FolderPath !has @"\ASUS\"
Response runbook
1) Triage: hash AsTaskSched.dll and confirm it is unsigned / not signed by ASUSTeK vs the article hashes. 2) Contain: isolate host, quarantine the DLL, and kill the RegSchdTask.exe process tree. 3) Hunt: check the same host/hour for outbound HTTPS to api.telegram.org and for a second sideload pair GoProAlertService.exe + pthreadVC2.dll.
DeviceImageLoadEvents
| where Timestamp > ago(30d)
| where InitiatingProcessFileName =~ "RegSchdTask.exe"
| where FileName =~ "AsTaskSched.dll"
| where not(FolderPath has_any (@"\Windows\System32\", @"\Program Files\"))
| project Timestamp, DeviceName, InitiatingProcessFileName, InitiatingProcessFolderPath, FileName, FolderPath, SHA256, MD5
